Q1_why_agg_degrades: Host-weighted aggregation replaces the tau_s-softmax weighting M2 was trained against with an exogenous, fixed HostScorer softmax. This inflates D_w substantially (M2: 0.0989->0.1692, +71%; K2: 0.1121->0.1902, +70%; J1: 0.1006->0.1217, +21%) while C_w actually DECREASES slightly for all three (M2: 0.4247->0.3933). Net damage (Agg_H-Agg_U) is dominated by the D_w inflation, and is largest for M2 (+7.42%) and K2 (+4.93%), smallest for J1 (+2.53%) -- the multi-slot, complementarity-optimized retrievers are hit hardest because HostScorer's own criterion doesn't know which slot was chosen for individual quality vs complementarity.
Q2_does_host_destroy_complementarity: No, not in the direct sense hypothesized. C_w does NOT re-increase under Host weighting for any retriever -- it decreases slightly. The 'damage' is driven by D_w inflation, not C_w reinflation. HostScorer weighting hurts individual-candidate quality more than it hurts complementarity.
Q3_residual_cosine_alignment: Moderate: M2's correction-target cosine is 0.166 (Uniform) / 0.158 (Host), comparable to K2's (0.166/0.165), both somewhat below J1's (0.187/0.182). Not low in absolute terms (clearly positive, real alignment) but modestly weaker than J1's.
Q4_oracle_gain_M2_vs_J1: No. J1's oracle gain (0.0588 U / 0.0583 H) exceeds M2's (0.0514 U / 0.0525 H), though M2 beats K2 under Uniform (0.0422) and is close to K2 under Host (0.0497). J1 has the best oracle potential of the three; M2 is a competitive second, not the best.
Q5_val_calibrated_lambda_M2_vs_J1: Nearly tied, M2 slightly worse. Uniform global-lambda test MSE: J1=0.463349, M2=0.463969 (gap 0.00062, negligible). Host global-lambda (matching TRACK-M's actual pipeline aggregation): J1=0.464746, M2=0.468076 (gap 0.0033, small but real) -- still MUCH smaller than the real trained-gate gap of 0.0098 with a CI entirely excluding zero.
Q6_primary_failure_cause: D. Mixed (A+B dominant, weak general C-type signal, not primary)
Q6_detail: A (aggregation mismatch) is real and measurably worse for M2 than J1 (+7.42% vs +2.53% damage), but does not devastate M2's ORACLE potential (oracle_fused_mse changes negligibly between Uniform and Host: 0.437398 vs 0.436336). B (gate/joint-training failure) is strongly suggested: a trivial, deployable, validation-calibrated single-lambda fusion already gets M2 within ~0.003-0.007 of J1's own calibrated result, dramatically closer than the real trained-gate's significant 0.0098 gap -- yet the conditional Gate-Only ablation (PART 18-19) was CONFOUNDED (frozen relation_mixer, never adapted to real nonzero retrieval, suppressed ALL three retrievers roughly equally, ~14x smaller improvement than full joint training for any arm) and only weakly/inconclusively supports B on its own. C (standalone-utility-never-tracks-downstream-utility) is weakly, generally true across ALL arms (retrieval_mse vs oracle_gain correlation is only 0.10-0.14 Pearson) but is NOT specifically why M2 underperforms J1 -- M2's downstream utility (oracle gain, calibrated-lambda result) is genuinely competitive with J1's, just not realized by the actual trained Stage2 pipeline.
Q7_detail: M2's retrieval is not fundamentally deficient for forecasting -- its oracle and validation-calibrated conditional utility are competitive with J1's. The evidence points to the STAGE2 CONSUMPTION pipeline (HostScorer aggregation choice, and/or joint mixer+gate training dynamics) as the primary bottleneck, not the M2 retrieval objective itself.
